tob-4056: The third volume of the Secret Doctrine gathers Blavatsky’s pieces on magic, signs, and the hidden side of the world’s faiths. Put together after her death, it roams from Kabbalah to the rites of old Egypt. Less tidy than the first two volumes, it teems with the startling claims that made her name.
tob-0156: James Darmesteter’s Zend-Avesta is the great French Englishing of Zoroaster’s writ — the hymns, laws, and holy doings of old Persia’s prophet. His foreword and notes brought the Avesta within western scholars’ reach. The work stays a landmark of Iran-learning.
tob-4156: A. P. Sinnett’s Esoteric Buddhism — drawn from the Mahatma Letters — bore Theosophy’s world-system to common eyes in 1883. Its rounds, root-breeds, and veiled masters caught Victorian minds athirst for eastern wisdom. The book launched Theosophy as a folk movement.
cia-0000108156: An April 1954 estimate of Indonesia's probable outlook through that year. Newly independent Indonesia was wobbling between democracy and disintegration, and Washington wanted a forecast. The document shows intelligence as prediction — analysts placing bets on another country's future with incomplete information.
cia-0000112356: A September 1989 summary of the Soviet TASS review of the central press for October 12. These digests showed what Moscow's editors chose to emphasize — and what they buried. Filed in the year the Berlin Wall fell, the entry is one more day's reading from the empire's final press.
cia-0000115456: A May 1986 interagency memo on prospects for leftist revolutionary groups in South America. With Central America burning, analysts looked south for the next front. The memo weighs whether the continent's guerrillas were a spent force or a gathering storm.
cia-0000119756: An October 1956 situation report on Hungary — one of dozens filed as the crisis consumed the intelligence community's attention. Each update layered new facts onto a fast-moving story. The document is a single frame in the most intensively reported Eastern European crisis of the decade.
cia-0000126956: A September 1966 report on the situation and prospects in Haiti. Five years into Papa Doc's reign of terror, the country was a prison with a flag. The document finds little to hope for — the prospects were as bleak as the situation.
cia-0000132156: Iraq-Kuwait Situation Report number 473, dated January 1991 — covering political developments including British parliamentary debate, the truncated title suggests. Numbered sitreps were the Gulf War's daily pulse. The entry is one heartbeat in the drumbeat toward Desert Storm.
cia-0000132656: A 1961 analysis of why the Cuban Revolution of 1958 led to Cuba's alignment with the USSR. The great question — was it inevitable? — examined in hindsight. The document is the autopsy: the revolution's path, explained.
cia-0000135956: A 1954 routing sheet with a LINCOLN cable explaining the need for urgent action — the truncated title cuts off what. The urgency, routed. The entry is the plea: the need, explained — the action, pending.
cia-0000136056: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on contacting a deleted person to work on the KUGOWN program. The recruit, unnamed; the program, coded. The entry is the recruitment: the contact, sought.
cia-0000136156: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on leaflet drops. Paper bombs over Guatemala. The document is the drop: the leaflets, scattered.
cia-0000136256: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK, from BRODFROST, reporting two F-47s passing over — the truncated title cuts off where. The fighters, sighted. The document is the overflight: the planes, seen.
cia-0000136356: An untitled 1954 document on a pact signed by Calligeris — without details except the pact, the truncated title suggests. The agreement, bare. The entry is the pact: the signature, noted — the terms, withheld.
cia-0000136856: A 1954 cable on following up the Martinez story, published in the latter part of January — the truncated title cuts off the year-part. The planted story, tracked. The document is the follow-up: the tale, pursued.
cia-0000136956: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on the C-124 aircraft schedule and cargo. The big lifters, timetabled. The document is the schedule: the cargo, planned.
un-ga-res-a-69-56: Resolution A/69/56, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The Assembly at work. The designation and year align; the content awaits.
un-sc-res-156: Security Council Resolution 156, adopted in 1960. The Council's crisis-year business. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1456: Security Council Resolution 1456, adopted in January 2003 — the counter-terrorism declaration, adopted at a foreign-ministers-level meeting, reaffirming the global fight against terrorism. The Council's ministers spoke as one. The resolution is the declaration: the fight, renewed.
un-sc-res-1656: Security Council Resolution 1656, adopted in 2006 — aligned. The mid-2000s Council at work. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1756: Security Council Resolution 1756, cataloged with the year 2003 — the numbering suggests 2007, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
cia-0000136756: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136756, date approximate. The circa papers. The document is the circa: the dating, estimated.
plos-pone-0000056: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: a low-protein diet increases hypoxic tolerance in Drosophila. Hungry fruit flies survive low oxygen better. The paper is the diet: the tolerance, raised.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d56: A memorandum by the Secretary of State, October 25, 1943 — Document 56. The department's internal thinking, on paper. The memo is the thinking: the secretary, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d156: The minister in Egypt, Kirk, to the chief of the Egyptian cabinet — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 156. Cairo's legation wrote the host government. The note is the host's: Kirk, to the cabinet.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d256: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 256. The editors' link. The note is the link: the story, continuous.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d356: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 356. The editors' link. The note is the link: the story, continuous.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d456: United States–United Kingdom agreed minutes, December 6, 1943 — Document 456. The shared record, another day. The minutes are the shared: the allies, agreed.
arxiv-2605-08856: Rolling a learned model forward step by step — predicting the future — often blows up: small errors amplify into nonsense. Adeel Pervez and Francesco Locatello show that controlling transient amplification tames those blowups and improves long-horizon rollouts. The 2026 paper is about keeping simulated futures on the rails.
arxiv-2605-08956: AI agents that run experiments and write papers sound like the future of science — but are they? Harshit Bisht, Vinay Kumar, Kevin Maik Jablonka, and colleagues argue that today's agentic AI scientists are not built for genuinely autonomous discovery. The 2026 paper is a critical reality check on the hype around robot scientists.
arxiv-2605-09156: Latin nouns had grammatical gender; as Latin became Occitan, the genders shifted in systematic ways. Ahan Chatterjee, Matthias Schöffel, Matthias Aßenmacher, and colleagues explore that shift computationally. The 2026 paper is historical linguistics on a thousand-year grammatical drift.
arxiv-2605-09856: Recovering 3D human meshes from images fails when bodies are occluded — motion priors fill the missing gaps. Tao Tang, Hong Liu, Xinshun Wang, and colleagues incorporate those priors with MoPO. The 2026 paper sees through occlusions using nothing but motion, cleverly.
arxiv-2605-10056: Learning parity with noise — hardness amplification for the sparse LPN problem. Divesh Aggarwal, Rishav Gupta, and Li Zeyong develop the amplification. The 2026 paper is cryptography on noisy parity. It amplifies cryptographic hardness from weak to strong.
plos-pone-0003456: Geneticists proposed a bold origin story for split genes in this 2008 paper. Eukaryotic genes are chopped into coding pieces separated by long non-coding stretches, and nobody knew why. The authors argued this fractured architecture could have arisen from random genetic sequences, offering a fresh hypothesis for one of molecular biology's oldest puzzles.
plos-pone-0003556: Neuroscientists Semir Zeki and John Paul Romaya scanned the brain on hate in this landmark 2008 study. Seventeen volunteers viewed faces of people they hated while lying in an fMRI scanner, and the team mapped the neural correlates of the emotion. The brain's hate circuit overlapped partly with romantic love's, suggesting passion's dark twin runs on neighboring machinery.
plos-pone-0003656: In 2008, a team showed a gene silencer shaping the growing brain. The protein REST, known for switching off neuron genes outside the brain, was found steering the mesh around cells as neurons form. By tuning that outer scaffold, REST helps guide stem cells into becoming neurons.
plos-pone-0003756: In 2008, Krintel, Osmark, and Larsen pinpointed the switches on a fat-burning enzyme. Two serine spots, 649 and 650, proved to be the main controls for protein kinase A activation of hormone-sensitive lipase. The precise mapping shows exactly where the body flips its fat-release switch.
plos-pone-0003856: In 2008, a team found exercise tuning the brain's hunger signals. Physical activity boosted how the brain's AMPK and mTOR energy sensors respond to leptin, the satiety hormone. The result shows exercise rewiring appetite control at the molecular level, not just burning calories.
plos-pone-0003956: In 2008, Eckmeier, Geurten, and Kress tracked how finches aim their eyes in flight. Free-flying zebra finches used gaze strategies tuned to optic flow. The study reveals the visual steering behind a bird's darting flight.
plos-pone-0004056: In 2008, Benn, Fisker, and Rodrigues found a birth vaccine acting differently by sex. Oral polio vaccine given with BCG at birth shifted infant mortality by sex. In Guinea-Bissau, the sex-differential effect challenged one-size-fits-all vaccine schedules. The surprising finding urges sex-aware design in newborn immunization programs.
plos-pone-0004156: In 2009, Watson, Ghodasra, and Platt linked a gene to monkey manners and moods. Serotonin transporter variants shaped social reward and punishment in rhesus macaques. Gene type tuned how monkeys valued social cues. The primate result echoes human social genetics closely.
plos-pone-0004256: In 2009, Sabado, Kavanagh, and Kaufmann replayed HIV's first strike in a dish. Lab priming recreated HIV-1-specific T cell responses seen in patients. The dish model showed fast loss of virus reactivity over time. The neat system speeds vaccine testing greatly.
plos-pone-0004356: In 2009, Pérez-Berná, Pabst, and Laggner probed viral membranes with short peptides. A peptide library was screened by DSC and SAXD against hepatitis C proteins directly. The heat and X-ray data matched the biology. The neat screen maps membrane-active regions well.
plos-pone-0358756: Flatworms can regrow a lost head, so scientists have wondered whether memories could survive the process. This paper reports a failure: repeated attempts to teach two flatworm species a simple learned response did not work, despite careful methods and historical precedent. The authors publish the negative result openly, arguing that failed experiments deserve a place in science — they stop others from repeating the same dead end.
plos-pone-0358056: Studying the eye’s pigment cells needs a steady supply — and sheep eyes are cheap and plentiful. This paper showed how to isolate uveal melanocytes from ovine eyes and grow them in 2D and 3D culture. The method gives eye researchers an accessible model for studying melanoma and eye disease.
plos-pone-0358356: Aging well takes more than doctor visits — it takes community. This study protocol laid out a trial evaluating community-based integrated care for functional decline and quality of life in middle-aged and older adults. Publishing the protocol first ensures the eventual results will be judged against a fixed plan.
plos-pone-0357156: Phone cameras bracket exposures to capture bright skies and dark shadows — then must fuse them cleanly. MEF-TBN is a three-branch neural network for multi-exposure image fusion that extracts features and enhances color. The approach produces sharper, more natural composite photos than older fusion methods.
plos-pone-0358556: A trained attendant at birth can mean the difference between life and death — yet many Bangladeshi mothers still deliver without one. This paper combined classic statistics with machine learning to map the prevalence and drivers of skilled birth attendance in Bangladesh. The findings point policymakers to the levers that actually get trained help to mothers.
plos-pone-0350956: Cancer survivors often face crushing loneliness after treatment ends. This paper published the protocol for a pilot trial testing an adapted social prescribing intervention — connecting survivors to community — against usual care. The feasibility pilot will show whether prescribing social life can heal what medicine leaves behind.
plos-pone-0355956: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency leaves lungs vulnerable to bronchiectasis — permanently widened airways. This study validated the Bronchiectasis Severity Index in these patients. The validated score gives doctors a tested tool for predicting who will fare worst.
plos-pone-0346756: Blood pooling between brain and skull can return after surgery. This paper used machine learning to classify recurrence risk after surgical treatment of chronic subdural hemorrhage. The model flags high-risk patients for closer follow-up.
plos-pone-0354756: Marbled pork tastes better — and Chinese and Western pigs marble differently. This integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analysis identified divergent regulatory networks for intramuscular fat in the two pig types. The networks reveal the molecular recipes behind marbling, guiding breeders.
plos-pone-0358456: Future sport managers need communication skills — and entrepreneurial drive to match. This paper tested career awareness as a mediator between communication skills and entrepreneurial tendencies in prospective sport managers. The mediation model shows how self-knowledge turns the ability to talk into the ability to build enterprises.
plos-pone-0357756: Newborns lose body heat dangerously fast — and mothers’ everyday practices decide survival. This qualitative descriptive study explored preventive practices against newborn hypothermia among post-natal mothers in Kilimanjaro’s public health facilities. The findings guide warming interventions that fit real mothers’ lives.
plos-pone-0355056: Sequencing short synthetic DNA strands quickly accelerates synthetic biology. OligoSeq enables rapid nanopore sequencing of single-stranded oligonucleotides. The streamlined method turns around oligo reads fast enough to keep pace with high-throughput DNA synthesis.
plos-pone-0354456: Acute myeloid leukemia urgently needs new drugs — and computation can accelerate the hunt. This paper prepared AML proteins for in silico drug design using pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. The computational pipeline shortens the road from protein structure to drug candidate.
plos-pone-0356356: Software developers handle personal data daily — but what makes them comply with privacy rules? This paper examined how legal awareness shapes developers’ data compliance behavior through a deterrence theory lens. The findings reveal that fear of punishment matters less than believed — with implications for how companies actually achieve compliance.
plos-pone-0343756: Cowpea — black-eyed pea — feeds millions, yet its varieties need genetic fingerprinting. This paper developed KASP molecular markers and constructed a fingerprinting system based on ddRAD sequencing. The genetic toolkit lets breeders and seed systems verify varieties — protecting farmers from mislabeled seed.
plos-pone-0355856: Children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia breathe the same polluted air as everyone else — with deadlier consequences. This Northern Thailand study linked air pollution to mortality in ALL patients across age groups from 1999 to 2020. The two-decade analysis adds childhood cancer to air pollution’s ledger of harm.
plos-pone-0356056: Frankincense trees — Boswellia sacra — are overharvested and poorly mapped. This paper combined spectral signature mapping with deep learning detection using WorldView-3 satellite imagery. The space-based census gives conservationists the first accurate maps of these culturally precious, ecologically threatened trees.
plos-pone-0355556: ‘Sexual harassment definitely involves a hierarchical transgression’ — European experts’ blunt framing. This paper analyzed key informants’ discourses on sexual harassment in European universities. The expert perspectives reveal how power — not just behavior — defines harassment in academic hierarchies.
plos-pone-0354856: Getting to cancer screening — transportation — shapes when cancer gets found. This scoping review examined transportation-related factors, screening, and stage at diagnosis. The findings expose how bus routes and car ownership quietly determine whether cancer is caught early or late.
plos-pone-0355156: Fetal growth restriction can starve babies of oxygen — and cord blood S100B might flag it. This prospective cohort study evaluated the protein’s concentration as a biomarker of fetal hypoxia in late growth restriction. The findings could give obstetricians a molecular alarm for babies in silent distress.
europmc-pmc2807856: Dirty air sends people to the ER, and this 2009 study pins down why they come. The team tied daily soot and its chemical parts to ER visits for each cause. Harm was not the same across ills. The split gives rule-makers proof for curbing the worst kinds of grime.
europmc-pmc2815756: Could short fasts make cancer treatment work better? This 2009 case series reports on patients who fasted around their chemotherapy sessions. The authors describe the cases and the rationale: fasting may protect healthy cells while sensitizing tumors. The early report was provocative rather than conclusive. It launched serious research into fasting as a companion to cancer therapy.
europmc-pmc2829056: A test's ROC curve measures its accuracy, but what does the area under it mean genetically? This 2010 paper works out the genetic interpretation of the area under the ROC curve in genomic profiling. The authors connect a statistics workhorse to genetics. Their framework helps researchers judge what genomic predictions can realistically achieve.
europmc-pmc2848556: A germ tenant in mosquitoes can bar dengue. This 2010 paper shows the lodger germ Wolbachia arms Aedes aegypti against the dengue virus. The team proves the guard in caged trials. The find loosed a keen living weapon against a virus with no cure.
europmc-pmc2868856: Risk numbers can wobble with study design, and this 2010 paper probes how much. The authors compare relative risk estimates from studies of the same population with different response rates and designs. Their probe quantifies the wobble. The work warns epidemiologists to mind their methods.
europmc-pmc2970556: The brain's immune cells prune synapses, guided by what eyes see. This 2010 paper shows microglial interactions with synapses are modulated by visual experience. The authors' imaging catches the pruning. Their work links experience to brain wiring. Dark-reared mice kept messier connections.
europmc-pmc3000156: A winter virus puts kids in hospital, this 2003 study finds. The authors report metapneumovirus infections among hospitalized children. Their work confirmed the germ as a real threat. The study guided testing. It ranks just behind RSV in tiny lungs. Winter wards brace for its return.
europmc-pmc6510456: Reading the full DNA of bacteria has let scientists watch drug-resistant germs evolve and spread almost in real time. This review shows how genome sequencing traces outbreaks, reveals how resistance genes move, and explains why some superbugs now defeat every drug doctors have. It is a tour of the genomic tools that hospitals use to fight back against untreatable infections.
europmc-pmc6611156: Pericytes - the shy cells hugging capillary walls - turn out to be key stagehands of brain blood flow. Known since the 1870s but long ignored, they regulate vessel tone, guard the blood-brain barrier, and falter in stroke and dementia. This review restores these wallflowers to their starring vascular role.
europmc-pmc6616856: Antibiotics do not vanish after use - they wash into rivers, soils, and farms, breeding resistance in the wild. This review traces antibiotic pollution from microbial ecology to public policy: how environmental drug residues select for superbugs and what rules could stem the flow. The fix needs ecologists and lawmakers together.
europmc-pmc6656856: Tiny RNA messengers circulate in blood - remarkably stable - and cancers leave their signature in them. This review weighs circulating microRNAs as cancer biomarkers: their promise for early detection and the hurdles, from noisy measurements to unclear origins. Liquid biopsy via microRNA is promising but unfinished.
europmc-pmc6688256: Flavonoids - the pigments behind autumn leaves and berry blues - are ancient plant inventions. Tracing their metabolism's evolution, this review shows how plants built the flavonoid toolkit over deep time. The story explains why these compounds are everywhere in the plant kingdom.
europmc-pmc6704256: Alzheimer's plaques may need microglia - the brain's immune cells - to take root. Wiping out microglia with a CSF1R-blocking drug, researchers watched plaque development stall in an Alzheimer's mouse model. The finding flips the script: the brain's defenders may unwittingly nurture the very plaques they surround.
europmc-pmc6723656: Yogurt, kimchi, kefir - fermented foods are having a moment. This review defines what counts as fermented, how these foods shift gut microbes, and what that means for digestion. The hype is real but uneven: some benefits are solid, others still need proof.
europmc-pmc6737756: Patients are research partners, not just subjects - but involving them well takes more than good intentions. This systematic review gathered frameworks for patient and public involvement in research, then co-designed a pilot putting them to the test. The result is practical guidance for making involvement real.
europmc-pmc6769656: Blood vessels are lined with living wallpaper - endothelial cells that do far more than contain blood. This update reviews vascular endothelial biology: how the cells regulate flow, clotting, and inflammation. The single-cell layer turns out to be a command center for circulation.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1156: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report surveys retiree benefits promised by state and local governments — pensions and health care for public workers. GAO examines benefit structures, legal protections, and the fiscal outlook for funding future costs. The report foreshadows the pension crises that would soon strain state budgets: promises made in good times coming due with too little saved.
gao-gaoreports-b-299456: Lockmasters Security Institute took its May 2007 lock-and-key contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call. The firm challenged the award; the ruling tests the claims. Security-training deals get the same fair-bid law as any buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-256: The SEC's computers needed steady hardening in 2007 — GAO's report says the market cop had to keep strengthening its controls year after year. The findings press for real persistence. The report's point: the guardian of the markets must guard its own gates.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-356: The coastal barrier lands got their status check in 2007 — GAO's report reviews the development and the federal aid that flowed there. The findings map the encroachment. The report's tension: the dunes the law meant to spare kept getting built on.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-156: The taxpayer's advocate was swamped in 2007, and GAO's report says the caseload had grown even as filers reported satisfaction. The findings balance the good news and the strain. The report asks whether the help desk for the harassed could keep up.
gao-gaoreports-b-299156: Free&Ben Inc. took its February 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call on the claims. The firm challenged the award, and the ruling tests the protest. Small firms get the same formal process as the giants.
openalex-w7206176456: School cafeterias throw away astonishing amounts of food, and this article reports a project that tackled the problem with small children. The Prato Consciente program at an early-childhood school in Juazeiro do Norte, Brazil, taught kids to waste less and compost what remains. The authors analyze what the intervention changed in behavior and awareness. A practical example of how environmental education can start at the lunch table.
openalex-w7205008356: Placing a PICC line, a long catheter threaded into a central vein, is delicate work that nurses increasingly do with ultrasound guidance. This integrative review gathers what research says about nurses inserting these lines with ultrasound help. The authors assess safety, success rates, and training needs. A clinical review at the intersection of nursing skill and imaging technology, where steadier hands mean safer patients.
openalex-w7204586256: Every cooking oil has a smoke point, the heat at which it starts to break down. This study compares the smoke point of oil from the American bullfrog, Rana catesbeiana, with a common reference oil. The authors test whether the frog oil stands up to kitchen heat. An offbeat food-science experiment probing an unusual ingredient's culinary potential.
openalex-w7204275056: Young gum trees grow better with help from soil fungi. This tree-farm study tested giving young eucalyptus plants friendly root fungi plus fermented natural fertilizer. The team measured how fast the seedlings grew and how strong they got. Hands-on research for nurseries that want hardier young trees.
pmc-13436956: A 2026 microbiome study in which scientists built custom communities of gut bacteria and used them to crowd out a lung pathogen in mice. By filling the ecological niches the pathogen needs, the designed probiotics kept it from taking hold. The experiment is an early step toward probiotic treatments that protect against infection rather than just aid digestion.
pmc-13451956: In this 2026 Italian study, researchers asked whether having a family history of chronic pain predicts a patient's current clinical picture. Family history turned out to carry real signal about pain severity and presentation. The finding supports asking about relatives' pain as part of routine assessment.
pmc-13452056: A 2026 computational biology paper predicting drug targets from perturbation transcriptomics — gene-activity changes after cells are disturbed — using a hypergraph siamese network guided by biological function. The model learns which proteins a compound likely hits. Smarter target prediction shortens the road from screen hit to real drug.
pmc-13449956: A 2026 chemistry paper on sensing synthon architectures — the recurring building blocks of crystal structures — with hyperfine-resolved rotational spectroscopy. The ultra-precise technique reads molecular shapes from their rotation. The work connects spectroscopy to crystal engineering.
pmc-13476356: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on vertebral alveolar echinococcosis diagnosed by metagenomic sequencing — "unmasking the mimic." Corrections formally amend the record. This entry preserves the correction as issued.
pmc-13589356: A 2026 paper using long-read RNA sequencing to map the isoform landscape — the full set of RNA variants — of the trigeminal ganglion in an allergic rhinitis mouse model. The facial nerve's molecular diversity underlies allergy symptoms. The map is a resource for the field.
pmc-13470256: This 2026 prospective cohort study found resting heart rate independently predicted major adverse cardiovascular events in hemodialysis patients. A simple vital sign carried prognostic weight. The finding supports its use in risk stratification.
pmc-13435356: A 2026 oncology paper using metabolomics to find biomarkers for early detection of immune-related adverse events in checkpoint inhibitor-treated patients. Predicting toxicity before it strikes could save lives. The metabolic markers are the advance.
pmc-13422256: In this 2026 cell biology paper, Ana1/Cep295 regulated centriole elongation via Cep135 and microtubules. The centriole assembly pathway was detailed. The regulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13587056: A 2026 data paper introducing AcousticSceneBD — real-world environmental audio for acoustic scene classification in Bangladesh. Local soundscapes train better models. The dataset is the resource.
pmc-13585456: In this 2026 lab medicine paper, improved criteria reduced unnecessary peripheral blood smear reviews by pathologists. Fewer manual reviews save expert time. The criteria are the efficiency gain.
pmc-13561956: A 2026 AI paper introducing VT-SCC — visual-text semantic alignment via multimodal guidance for unified staple crop organ counting. Counting wheat heads by AI got a multimodal boost. The framework is the contribution.
pmc-13530656: A 2026 conference poster finding pre-operative patient-reported outcomes predicted time to return to sport in NCAA Division I athletes after hip arthroscopy. The surveys forecasted recovery. The poster validates the prediction.
pmc-13544056: A 2026 protocol and preliminary results for evaluating augmented reality in interstitial brachytherapy optimization — a prospective phantom-based study. AR guided the radioactive seeds. The phantom study is the first test.
pmc-13506356: In this 2026 pharmaceutics paper, a caffeine and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid cocrystal hydrate was prepared, characterized, and evaluated. The cocrystal engineering is the work. The evaluation is the data.
pmc-13389356: This 2026 paper presented an ion treatment planning framework including nanodosimetric ionization detail through cluster dose. The proton therapy planning was refined. The framework is the advance.
pmc-13354256: This 2026 editorial, "From Evidence to Practice," bridged the implementation gap. The commentary urges translation. The editorial is the call.
pmc-13500156: In this 2026 extended follow-up of the NIHP2019 trial, hypothermic oxygenated perfusion was compared to standard treatment of donor hearts in heart transplantation. The perfusion's long-term benefits were tested. The follow-up is the evidence.
pmc-13466956: In this 2026 paper, the therapeutic impact of tirzepatide in people with partial lipodystrophy was evaluated. The GLP-1 drug's rare-disease role was tested. The impact is the preliminary evidence.
pmc-13473156: This 2026 systematic review, pairwise meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis prioritized chemotherapy-anchored regimens after EGFR-TKI failure in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (the title is truncated). The post-TKI options were ranked. The prioritization guides oncologists.
pmc-13467556: This 2026 paper improved a BP neural network ensemble model for asphalt pavement performance prediction. The road's future was forecasted. The improving is the engineering.
pmc-13427856: A 2026 paper with long-term clinical outcomes and quality of life after TESAR — totally endoscopic sublay anterior repair for diastasis recti and ventral hernias (the title is truncated). The endoscopic repair's durability was reported. The outcomes are the evidence.
pmc-13495956: A 2026 physics paper on quantitative infrared-to-terahertz nanospectroscopy of semiconductors. The nanoscale spectra were quantified. The nanospectroscopy is the tool.
pmc-13441256: A 2026 case report: "Caught in the Whirl" — midgut volvulus in an elderly patient. The twisted bowel's whirl sign was the clue. The case teaches the emergency.
pmc-13453456: A 2026 protocol for automated optimization of feature selection and clustering parameters in single-cell RNA-seq using scAutoTune. The single-cell analysis was auto-tuned. The protocol is the computational method.
pmc-13520656: A 2026 biology education paper: "Is Tori seeing red?" — a first-year lesson unveiling phenotypic variation's complexity with pedigree analysis. The color vision lesson taught genetics. The lesson is the pedagogy.
pmc-13625856: A 2026 paper on regulation and function of Sox2 and CD44 expression in the stomach by bone morphogenetic protein signaling. The gastric stemness was regulated. The function is the developmental insight.
pmc-13524556: This 2026 paper showed bile acid profiles defined disease-specific cholestatic states in primary sclerosing and primary biliary cholangitis. The bile acids distinguished the diseases. The defining is the diagnostic advance.
pmc-13467456: This 2026 cardiology paper offered clinical perspectives on vericiguat in elderly heart failure patients with reduced ejection fraction — from pathophysiology to implementation. The drug's geriatric role was examined. The perspectives guide cardiologists.
pmc-13420356: In this 2026 paper, abortion was briefly described — the evolution of methods. The historical overview is the contribution. The description is the reference.
arxiv-2606-15956: Machine learning models usually need lots of carefully labeled images or strict assumptions to learn good visual features. This paper shows a simpler path: learning from how things change over time in video. By comparing consecutive frames, the model builds strong image understanding with far fewer assumptions — work from a team including AI researcher Yann LeCun.
arxiv-2606-16156: Cell skins are built of fats, yet labs can also weave skin-like sheets from mixed stuff. This paper charts how ultra-thin mixed sheets — fats plus chain-plastics — shift shape as settings change. The news aids bio-builders who craft fake cell skins and drug pods.
arxiv-2606-16756: Multiple sclerosis (MS) scars the brain, and 'paramagnetic rim lesions' — scars with iron rims — flag aggressive disease. This paper classifies those lesions in 3D from MRI scans, fusing two scan types (QSM and FLAIR) with an asymmetric model. It is for neuroimaging researchers tracking MS.
arxiv-2606-16856: Teaching robots from human preferences needs feedback — and feedback is expensive. This paper makes it feedback-efficient with video-based optimal transport for offline preference-based RL. It is for robotics researchers learning from limited human input. Less asking, more learning. Every clip counts.
